messages.subject: Model selection leading to different conclusions
parts:
Hi!

I know INLA isn't really designed for model selection but anyhow..... On a few occasions, I have a situation where the 95% CI of a model coef for a variable don't overlap zero but when I compare DIC or calculate Bayes factor between models with and without the variable, they tell me there is no support for the variable. I think I trust more the 95% CIs but then I am not sure why I am being lead to different conclusions.

An example is below in which the variable of interest is sprevwtemps

there is nothing automatic here, and no criteria that works uniformly
best. 

maybe this paper will be useful

waic is available in INLA using control.compute=list(waic=TRUE)


Best

messages.author: 6e4e10e46624db56
messages.subject: Re: Model selection leading to different conclusions
parts:
Dear Rue

Is it possible for the DIC and Bayes factor leads to the different conclusion? I tried to estimate the spatiotemporal model. I got different conclusion between DIC and Bayes Factor. I calculated the Bayes Factor based on the ration of the exp(Marginal log-Likelihood). 

Thank you

Best Regards
Mindra

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Model selection leading to different conclusions
parts:
Yes.

Definitively.

Every model comparison criteria has a different definition of "better" or "best".

Personally, I suggest computing several different criteria and only reporting a strong conclusion when they all agree on the result.

PS: If you use marginal likelihoods, make sure you have no intrinsic components, or adjust for them (see e.g. inla.doc("rw2")).

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka

See inla.doc("Besag"), the note at the bottom of the document.

The easiest is to use DIC and WAIC and CPO, and some cross-validation. (And forget about mlik)

Haakon
